check.finding: The city inventory's 2024 total is 47,944,551 tCO2e (47.94 million metric tonnes) and OWID gives Denmark 45,938,950 tCO2e for 2024; 45.94 / 47.94 = 0.958. Both are metric tonnes CO2e, but the city's GPC inventory and OWID's national series (Jones et al., including land use) are built on different scopes, so the comparison is approximate.

items.sentence: hauls away an Eiffel Tower of trash and recycling every day

nyc.label: Trash, recycling and compost collected by DSNY per day
nyc.quote: DSNY collects 24 million pounds of trash, recycling, and compostable material every day.

match.label: Total weight of the Eiffel Tower

items.note: Department of Sanitation about page ('24 million pounds of trash, recycling, and compostable material every day', converted to metric tonnes); the Eiffel Tower's official key figures (10,100 tonnes total, 7,300 of it the metal frame).

check.finding: 24 million pounds is 10,886 metric tonnes and the tower's official total weight is 10,100 tonnes (the French site's figure is metric); 10100 / 10886 = 0.928. The DSNY figure includes compostable material as well as trash and recycling.

items.sentence: has as many restaurants and cafes as there are KFCs in the world
items.caveat: Every food-service place the Health Department inspects, including bars that serve food and college cafeterias.

nyc.label: Active restaurants in DOHMH's inspection database (distinct CAMIS IDs)
nyc.quote: [{"count_distinct_camis":"31304"}]

match.label: KFC restaurants in the entire world

items.note: Distinct establishments in the Health Department's restaurant inspection dataset on NYC Open Data (active status, inspected in the last three years), queried Sept. 3, 2026; KFC's worldwide unit count at Dec. 31, 2025 from Yum! Brands' fourth-quarter earnings release filed with the SEC. Pinned at Louisville, KFC's home.

check.finding: The DOHMH inspection dataset returns 31,304 distinct establishments and Yum's 8-K exhibit gives 33,897 KFC restaurants at year end 2025; 33,897 / 31,304 = 1.083. The DOHMH count covers all inspected food-service establishments (bars, cafes, cafeterias), not restaurants alone.

items.sentence: has as many hotel rooms as Orlando

nyc.label: Average monthly active hotel rooms in New York City
nyc.quote: In 2025, the number of average monthly active hotel rooms was 124,000, up 1.9 percent from 2024 (121,700).

match.label: Hotel rooms in Orlando
match.quote: With more than 130,000 hotel rooms, 47,000 vacation rentals and 26,000 timeshare properties, Orlando offers special accommodations for every visitor.

items.note: State Comptroller's July 2026 report on the city's hotel industry (average monthly active rooms in 2025; about 16,000 rooms used as shelter are excluded); Visit Orlando's press kit for the destination. Las Vegas is larger (about 150,000) but no fetched page stated its total.

check.finding: Both figures verified; 130,000 / 124,000 = 1.048. The Orlando figure is Visit Orlando's rounded promotional number for its multi-county destination area, while the New York figure is active rooms only; the same OSC report notes the city had over 127,000 rooms in January 2020.

items.sentence: speaks as many languages as Indonesia
items.caveat: The city count is language varieties across the metro area; Indonesia's is distinct living languages.

nyc.label: Language varieties spoken in the New York metropolitan area
nyc.quote: ELA has mapped 700-plus language varieties (and counting) to over 1200 significant sites around the metropolitan area

match.label: Living languages of Indonesia (Ethnologue)
match.quote: Indonesia: 710 languages ... This data is from the Ethnologue dataset produced by the Summer Institute of Linguistics International

items.note: Endangered Language Alliance's New York City language map ('700-plus language varieties'); Ethnologue's 2024 count for Indonesia as cited by Our World in Data. Papua New Guinea (840) is outside the band.

check.finding: Both figures verified; 710 / 700 = 1.014. ELA counts 'language varieties' across the metropolitan area (not the city alone) and '700-plus' is a floor, whereas Ethnologue counts distinct living languages, so the two are not the same unit.

items.sentence: files as many 311 requests a year as the country of Georgia has people

nyc.label: 311 service requests filed in New York City, calendar 2025

items.note: Count of 2025 service requests in the 311 dataset on NYC Open Data; Georgia's 2023 population from Our World in Data. The State Comptroller corroborates 2024 at 'over 3.4 million'.

check.finding: The 311 dataset returns 3,655,040 service requests created in 2025 and OWID's population file gives Georgia 3,807,494; 3,807,494 / 3,655,040 = 1.042. The Georgia figure is for 2023, the latest year in the OWID file, not 2024.

items.sentence: runs as many public library outlets as all of Maryland
items.caveat: Outlets, not just branch buildings: the count includes 3 central libraries and 5 books-by-mail outlets, against Maryland's 15 and 24.

nyc.label: Public library outlets run by New York City's three systems
nyc.quote: Outlet records with FSCSKEY NY0778 (NEW YORK PUBLIC LIBRARY, THE BRANCH LIBRARIES) 85, NY0562 (QUEENS BOROUGH PUBLIC LIBRARY) 64, NY0004 (BROOKLYN PUBLIC LIBRARY) 57, totalling 206: 3 central, 198 branch, 5 books-by-mail (column C_OUT_TY)

match.label: Every public library outlet in Maryland
match.quote: Outlet records with STABR MD total 218: 15 central, 179 branch, 24 books-by-mail (column C_OUT_TY)

items.note: Both counts are row counts of one federal file, the Institute of Museum and Library Services Public Libraries Survey for fiscal 2024, so central libraries, branches and books-by-mail outlets are counted the same way on both sides. New York City runs three separate systems: the New York Public Library across the Bronx, Manhattan and Staten Island, plus Brooklyn and Queens. Vermont (190), Oklahoma (223) and Oregon (225) were the next closest states.

check.finding: Both row counts (206 and 218) and the 218/206 = 1.058 ratio are verified directly from the IMLS FY2024 outlet file. The claim calls these 'branches,' but the counted rows are all outlet types in the file, including 3 central libraries and 5 bookmobile/mobile-service outlets on the NYC side and 15 central libraries and 24 bookmobile/mobile-service outlets on the Maryland side, not fixed branch buildings only.

items.sentence: has as many murders a year as Houston
items.caveat: Houston's count is homicides reported to its police. Houston has 2.4 million people to New York City's 8.5 million, so its rate is about three times higher.

nyc.label: Murders in New York City, 2025
nyc.quote: Across the city, murder declined by 20.2% (305 vs. 382), with 77 fewer murders compared to 2024.

match.label: Homicides in Houston, 2025
match.quote: Between 2024 and 2025, the number of homicides reported to the Houston Police Department declined from 331 to 272, according to year-end data gleaned through an open records request.

items.note: NYPD year-end 2025 release (murder and non-negligent manslaughter); Houston Police Department 2025 homicide count obtained by the Houston Chronicle through a records request and syndicated on Yahoo News. Houston is 11 percent lower, the widest gap on this page; Memphis (235) and Philadelphia (222) were further off. Populations from Census Vintage 2024.

check.finding: Both figures verified; 272 / 305 = 0.892, the widest gap in this batch. Houston's count is homicides reported to HPD (which can include justifiable homicides) rather than murders, and 'as many' stretches an 11 percent difference.

items.sentence: has as many people shot each year as Philadelphia
items.caveat: Philadelphia has 1.57 million people; its per-capita rate is more than five times higher.

nyc.label: Shooting victims in New York City, 2025
nyc.quote: The number of people shot in New York City also fell to a historic low in 2025 with 856 shooting victims citywide.

match.label: Shooting victims in Philadelphia, 2025
match.quote: Shooting incidents decreased 29% from last year, to 826 shootings, and the number of shooting victims recorded fell by 16%, to 906 people.

items.note: NYPD year-end 2025 release; Philadelphia Police data as reported by WHYY on Dec. 31, 2025, running through Dec. 30.

check.finding: Both figures verified; 906 / 856 = 1.058. The Philadelphia article was written in the last days of 2025 (it gives homicides 'as of Tuesday night'), so 906 is a near-year-end count that may not match the final tally.

items.sentence: has as many police officers as all of Austria
items.caveat: Uniformed headcount at the end of fiscal 2025; the department is hiring toward 35,555 by the end of 2026.

nyc.label: NYPD uniformed officers, end of FY2025

match.label: All police officers in Austria, Dec. 2025
match.quote: Österreich hat nun mit über 32.500 Exekutivbediensteten so viele Polizistinnen und Polizisten wie nie zuvor im Dienst.

items.note: NYPD uniformed personnel at the end of fiscal 2025 from the Mayor's Management Report; Austria's Interior Ministry 2025 personnel figure ('over 32,500 Exekutivbedienstete') as reported by 5min.at. The alternate match is the Royal Navy and Royal Marines' regular strength, 32,520.

check.finding: The MMR gives 33,614 uniformed NYPD personnel for fiscal 2025 and the Austrian article says over 32,500 police officers as of December 2025; 32,500 / 33,614 = 0.967. The Austrian figure is a rounded 'over 32,500' from a regional news site reporting the Interior Ministry's number.

items.sentence: loses as many people to traffic crashes as all of Sweden

nyc.label: Traffic deaths in New York City, 2025
nyc.quote: There were 205 recorded traffic deaths in 2025, a 19 percent decline from 253 fatalities last year

match.label: Road deaths in Sweden, 2025
match.quote: Under 2025 omkom 203 personer i olyckor i vägtrafiken

items.note: Department of Transportation's 2025 Vision Zero year-end release; Trafikanalys (Sweden's official transport statistics agency) release on 2025 road deaths. Ireland (185) is the backup.

check.finding: Both figures verified; 203 / 205 = 0.990. Sweden's official count excludes 42 further road deaths ruled suicides, which is the standard practice for its statistics.

items.sentence: holds as many people in jail as Switzerland holds in all its prisons
items.caveat: Fiscal 2025 average; the jail population passed 7,000 later in 2025.

nyc.label: NYC jail average daily population, FY2025
nyc.quote: The average daily population (ADP) in Fiscal 2025 was 6,823, an increase of nearly 10 percent from Fiscal 2024.

items.note: Department of Correction average daily population for fiscal 2025 from the Mayor's Management Report; Switzerland's total prison population at Jan. 31, 2026 per World Prison Brief, citing the Swiss Federal Statistical Office. The Board of Correction's January 2026 report gives a fiscal 2026 year-to-date average of 7,247.

check.finding: Both figures verified; 7,119 / 6,823 = 1.043. New York's is a fiscal-year average and Switzerland's is a single-day count, but both cover the whole detained population including pretrial.

items.sentence: answers as many 911 calls a year as Arizona has people

nyc.label: 911 calls to the NYPD, FY2025

items.note: NYPD 911 calls in fiscal 2025 from the Mayor's Management Report; Arizona population, Census Bureau Vintage 2024.

check.finding: The MMR gives 7,492,892 total 911 calls in fiscal 2025 and the Census release gives Arizona 7,582,384; 7,582,384 / 7,492,892 = 1.012. The New York figure is for the fiscal year ending June 2025.

items.sentence: makes as many arrests a year as Buffalo has people

nyc.label: NYPD arrests, calendar 2025

match.label: Population of Buffalo, N.Y.
match.quote: With 276,854 people, Buffalo is the 6th most populated city in the state of New York out of 1,522 cities according to the most current US Census data.

items.note: Row count of 2025 arrests in the NYPD Arrests Data (Historic) dataset on NYC Open Data, all ages; Buffalo population, Census Vintage 2024, via a secondary site (the Census QuickFacts page blocks automated fetches).

nyc.quote: Emergency medical incidents (ambulances) 1,388,043 1,531,959 1,613,316 1,644,446 1,615,531 * * Up *
